transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. It's like I can’t just sit idle. And, well, we have a new setup at work recently, and it's made that a lot harder for me to hide.

Can you tell me whether this feeling of always needing to move or switch tasks has been part of your life since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently, say in the past few months or years?

It's definitely been around since I was a kid, long before this recent job change. I remember back in grade school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. They said I talked out of turn a lot and constantly had to be reminded to just stay focused on my work. So, yeah, it's not a new thing for me at all.
Do you often feel physically restless or fidgety, like you need to get up and move, or find yourself blurting things out or acting impulsively without thinking?

Yeah, I do. Like, if I have to sit still through a long training video at work, or if I'm stuck in a slow appointment, I start to feel kind of boxed in. I just get this feeling where I really need to stand up, stretch, or at least do something with my hands. It's just tough for me to sit there and do nothing.
Besides the restlessness, do you often find yourself losing track of details, forgetting things, or having trouble staying focused on tasks like reading a report or following a conversation?

Yeah, that definitely happens. Like at work, I’ll think I’ve completely finished a customer ticket and moved on. But then, later on, I'll notice I typed the wrong account number, or maybe I skipped one of the required boxes on the screen. Or I just missed one little instruction, and that makes the whole thing come back to me to fix. It's just... small details like that slipping past me.
Aside from work, have these issues with focus, restlessness, or impulsivity also caused problems in other areas of your life, like at home or in your relationships?

Yeah, it does happen at home, too. Even with just... quiet stuff that’s supposed to relax me. Like, if I try reading, or if I'm sitting through a movie with my wife, it usually doesn’t last long. Pretty soon I’m shifting around in my seat, making comments, or just getting up to go grab something. So, yeah, it definitely makes it hard for us to just unwind together.
Have you ever had distinct periods where, along with the restlessness, you also felt unusually euphoric, needed much less sleep, or had racing thoughts, separate from your everyday baseline?

No, I can't say I've ever felt like that. I mean, the restlessness is just kind of how I always am. I don't get these highs where I'm super happy or feel like I don't need to sleep. My sleep is pretty normal, and I don't really have racing thoughts like you're describing. It's just the usual fidgeting and having a hard time sitting still.
